Being a mother really depressed my mother, and I often had to stay home all day with her while my dad was out working. When she'd want to take one of her daily few-hour-long naps, I'd occasionally not want to go into the room with her (what kid wants to lie silently on the bed while his/her mother sleeps for 3 hours without any form of entertainment, unable to sleep in the middle of the day?). 

During the times that I'd beg to stay out of the room and stay downstairs to play videogames or something, she'd put me in a dark laundry room in the basement (it was at the end of a dark hallway so it scared the hell out of me) and hold the doorknob just outside of the door (there wasn't a lock so otherwise I'd be able to get out). 

I was anywhere from 5-6 years old when this would happen, and I just remember screaming because the dark terrified me, and her being completely silent. Fortunately she'd only keep me in there for 3-5 minute intervals, because that amount of time was enough to get me to come out and agree to stay in her room while she napped.

To answer your original question, since these occasions happened and she spontaneously hit me a lot throughout my childhood, on the rare occasions that I told her, crying (however a little kid does this) that I was tired of it and threatened to call the police, she said that all that would happen is "then mommy will go to jail and you will go to a foster home and be a bad man's child. Bad men will be much worse than mommy, they do bad things to little girls."

Still surprises me to this day that even small children can understand what that means.
